3.05 Gyr ago: only 3.2 TW leaves the core, less than the 5.6 TW conduction carries along its adiabat, so the liquid iron no longer convects.
The core's centre cooled to the iron alloy's melting point (4153 K at 180 GPa), 1.23 Gyr ago: a solid inner core starts to grow, letting out latent heat and light elements that stir the liquid above.
1.23 Gyr ago: 2.0 TW leaves the core, less than the 5.4 TW conduction carries along its adiabat, but light elements let out as it freezes add the buoyancy of 4.8 TW.

core.why_now: A dynamo runs: 1.8 TW leaves the core against 5.4 TW conducted along its adiabat, field about 1135 μT inside the core.

findings.why: Earth crosses the star every 365.3 days, dimming it by 84 ppm for 13.1 hours; 10 crossings in the watch against 2 ppm of noise over that time gives 53.1σ.

Earth swings the star towards and away from here by 0.089 m/s every 365.3 days; 877 measurements at 1.00 m/s (with the star's own 1.0 m/s jitter) give 1.3σ. Only the minimum mass is measured: the tilt is unknown.
From here Jupiter's orbit is tilted 1.281° from edge-on; it would need to be within 0.056° to cross the star's face, so it never transits.

Jupiter swings the star towards and away from here by 12.472 m/s every 4332.4 days; 877 measurements at 1.00 m/s (with the star's own 1.0 m/s jitter) give 184.6σ. Only the minimum mass is measured: the tilt is unknown.

epochs.name: Recombination
epochs.why: the universe cools below about 3000 K at z = 1092: electrons and protons combine into hydrogen and light runs free, the background we now see as the CMB (Hu and Sugiyama 1996 fit to Omega_b h^2 and Omega_m h^2)

epochs.name: Dark ages
epochs.why: neutral gas and no stars yet; overdensities grow in proportion to the growth factor D(a)

epochs.name: First stars
epochs.why: the first 1e6 solar-mass minihaloes from 3-sigma peaks collapse at z = 17.3 (D sigma(M) nu = 1.686): Population III stars light up

epochs.name: Reionisation (half way)
epochs.why: half the intergalactic hydrogen is ionised at z = 7.7: zeta = 11 times the mass in haloes able to cool by atomic hydrogen (Planck 2018 measure z = 7.8 +- 0.7 with BAO, 7.7 +- 0.7 without)

epochs.name: Reionisation complete
epochs.why: the last neutral pockets are gone by z = 6.2; haloes below the filtering mass can no longer gather gas, leaving fossil dwarfs

epochs.name: Cosmic noon
epochs.why: the universe forms stars fastest at z = 1.86 (Madau and Dickinson 2014); since then the rate has fallen about tenfold

epochs.name: Now
epochs.why: the pack's present, 13.8 Gyr after the origin; dark energy now dominates and expansion accelerates

epochs.name: Last stars form
epochs.why: gas is used up and star formation ends; the longest-lived red dwarfs shine on (Adams and Laughlin 1997)

epochs.name: Degenerate era
epochs.why: white dwarfs, neutron stars, brown dwarfs and black holes hold almost all the baryons; occasional collisions make new stars (Adams and Laughlin 1997)

epochs.name: Black hole era
epochs.why: protons decay (lifetime 1e37 years in this pack) and degenerate matter dissolves; only black holes remain (Adams and Laughlin 1997)

epochs.name: Dark era
epochs.why: the largest black holes (1e11 solar masses) evaporate by Hawking radiation; photons, leptons and dark energy remain

model: matter: the cell's mass from the web's density; dark and ordinary in the universe's shares
haloes: the catalogued ones (G2) and, below the floor, the same mass function down to floor_low_msun; the rest of the dark matter never collapsed into those
